correctness.rationale: An explicit closed-neighbourhood adjacency list for h, x_{r,i}, y_{ij} yields an if-and-only-if domination criterion in terms of columns T,S,U and selected within-part edges E. Hub-selected sets are enumerated by a forced clique; hub-omitted sets use inclusion-exclusion for degree-positive vertices, separating t>=2 and t<=1. The cardinality lower bounds and equality cases classify all minimum sets. Exact independently constructed token-graph brute force checked every coefficient and hub split for n=2..5 (2,131,008 subsets), and exact formula checks extended to n=11. The proof covers all n>=2; finite tests are supporting rather than substitutive.

originality.rationale: The 2026 token-graph preprints already give domination number n, and the October 22 manuscript Lemma 2.2 characterizes feasible sets in general K_{m,n}. The proposed NEW claim is the closed labelled domination polynomial for all cardinalities, the exact multiplicity n(n+3)2^{n-3} of optimal sets for n>=5 with 9,33,80 at n=2,3,4, and the sharp threshold that all optimal sets contain h precisely for n>=5. value.rationale: Ordinary domination number alone leaves a natural unbounded graph family of minimum certificates and all valid cardinalities uncounted. The exact polynomial provides every labelled coefficient and separates hub-present from hub-absent solutions; the cutoff at n=5 and explicit optimum multiplicities exhibit a meaningful structural transition not inferable from the known minimum number. This is a complete enumerative invariant of a canonical token graph family, not a sample computation or arbitrary truncation.
